Charging the exact same price as the registry wholesale price. This could totally throw all registrars out of competition for the price of registry wholesale price.

One drawback to using Cloudflare Registrar that wasn't obvious to me at first is that you have to use Cloudflare's nameservers... I've chosen to pay an extra $0.50 or so per domain to Porkbun for the option of using other nameservers.

I've moved some domains to Cloudflare Registrar not knowing this limitation... I've also had a billing issue with Cloudflare Registrar. I transferred two domains and paid the renewal fee, and two months later was charged for the same domains again.

My experience with Registrar has been 4/5 okay and 1/5 horrible so far... Registrar has now charged me $90 (.io domain is $45/year) for a domain _which they do not control_, and this has obviously not been reflected in the domain expiration date.
Note that for some reason, Cloudflare charges substantially more for .io domains than other registrars. Cloudflare charges $45 whereas Dynadot charges $26.99 and Porkbun charges $28.97.
New GTLDs may cost considerably more at Cloudflare Registrar. For example, the annual cost of a .space domain during transfer is $15.18... while renewal for the same domain at Namecheap costs $9.06.

I had a good experience moving a domain to Cloudflare, but one thing is still bugging me: To allow a third party to modify the DNS you have to use an API key that has full access to modify everything in your Cloudflare account.
I transferred one domain to Cloudflare, and I didn't have any issues. I admit that it's just one data point, but I am happy.
The major issue with this is that the transferred domain must use CloudFlare NS and be on the platform. Really not worth the lock-in for like $1/year you save off other places.

It's been a few months since launch, but I still can't use my own nameservers for the domains. While the registry-pricing can often workout cheaper, some registrars negotiate nicer deals with the registry.
They don't support even .us, which is a pity. When I start a new project, I register with another registrar and wait 60 days to move it to Cloudflare - what a nonsense!

Contact information is redacted by default. I've moved a bunch of domains over, they're all redacted in the whois without me taking any action... All the transfers from GoDaddy to Cloudflare went super smooth, took minutes.
.app Support too! Made the switch already, fast and cheaper than what I was paying at Google.
Too bad they don't support custom name servers.
Still no support for IDN domains though..
Cloudflare is also the largest authoritative DNS deployment in the world, and changes propagate in closer to 15 seconds than 15 minutes. We do support WHOIS Privacy, free of charge.
